explanation: Maintain the farthest reachable index while scanning only reachable positions. Extend that boundary with each jump and succeed once it reaches the final index.
timeComplexity: O(n) time for n positions. Each index is inspected at most once and the farthest boundary update is constant time.
spaceComplexity: O(1) auxiliary space. The scan index and farthest reachable index are scalars.
attribution: Original EPI Practice C# implementation, reusing and refining the repository-authored Blind75 algorithm fixtures. Collection membership follows Crackr; no external solution service is used.
correctness: All indices up to farthest are reachable from the start. Processing any reachable index extends that boundary to include every position permitted by its jump. If the next index exceeds the boundary, no later index can be reached; reaching the final index proves success.
walkthrough: For [2,0,1,0], the first value reaches index 2. Index 1 adds no range, but index 2 extends reach to 3, the last index. Return true.
edgeCases: A singleton array is already at its final index.
A zero can block progress only when no earlier jump passes it.
Jumps may choose any distance up to the current value.
